context:
Goal: a triage session on your Mac does triage's work, roadmap pushes included, as cloud triage does.
Problem (rule): it is not a feature we chose for the cloud. A guard proves a session's tier from that session's own service record, and only cloud sessions carry tags there; the coordinator sets them, and Claude inside the session cannot change them. A Mac session you start has no tag store, so nothing can prove its tier, and the guard refuses its roadmap push.
Based on (read): the guard reads tags from get_session; only owner-typed words such as override and opus are proof Claude cannot forge.
Departs from: main, where only cloud tags prove a tier — a adds an owner word; b adds a tier file only your computer writes.

lastAnswer.note: Asked: "why is this a cloud exclusive feature?". Rewritten 22:22 CST: explains why only the cloud tag is proof.

options.gain: Mac triage pushes the roadmap like cloud triage.
options.how: You type 'tier triage' in a Mac session to mark it triage; 'tier off' ends it. It is stored in a state folder Claude cannot write.
options.label: Owner word 'tier triage'

options.gain: No word to type each time.
options.how: The Mac session reads its tier from a file that only your computer's setup writes, never Claude.
options.label: A tier file your computer writes
options.lose: A setup step on each Mac, and a file to keep current.

options.how: Mac triage hands each roadmap push to cloud triage.
options.label: No fix
options.lose: Mac triage depends on a cloud triage being up.

title: A Mac session cannot prove it is triage, because only the cloud attaches a tag Claude cannot fake: add your 'tier triage' word, or keep roadmap pushes in the cloud?
why: Recommended: a. It gives a Mac session the same proof the cloud's tag gives, from words only you can type.
